A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OFM research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original GP/TGP regression comparisons in Table 1 and original prior-learning and posterior-sampling experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these experiments and adds kernel comparisons, optimal-transport ablations, and trace-estimator measurements in Tables 2, 7, and 8.

M1.justification: The FNO backbone, optimal-transport conditional flow-matching objective, Hutchinson likelihood estimation, and GP-space SGLD sampling remain unchanged. Algorithms 1 and 2 retain their procedures; alternative-path discussions and experimental ablations do not establish a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix N adds synthetic 1D GP regression using nonstationary Gibbs and Rational Quadratic kernels, extending the represented process distributions beyond the original Matérn examples. The existing GP/TGP, co-domain GP, Navier-Stokes, black-hole, MNIST-SDF, and resolution-transfer coverage is retained.

E2.justification: ConvCNP is added to the original Table 1 comparison and to the Navier-Stokes, black-hole, and MNIST-SDF visual comparisons in Figures 2, 5, and 8. The previous comparator set is retained; renaming neural processes as conditional models does not introduce additional methods.

E3.justification: The original training and regression settings in v1 Tables 2–5 are retained in v3 Tables 3–6. Added protocols evaluate coupling choices using 1,000 real/generated Navier-Stokes samples, density/autocovariance/spectral MSE, training loss, and function evaluations, and compare GP likelihood estimates against direct Jacobian-trace integration.

E4.justification: v1 lacks direct experimental tests of the coupling choice and trace-estimator variability. Appendix P adds independent-versus-optimal coupling ablation, optimal-transport batch-size scaling, and Hutchinson noise-sample scaling against exact likelihood calculations, substantially expanding component validation.

E5.justification: Appendix P newly reports 100 repetitions for each trace-estimator noise count, repeated across five GP samples, with means and standard deviations in Table 8 and Figure 25. This adds Monte Carlo uncertainty reporting beyond the posterior uncertainty already shown in v1; repeated-training or benchmark-seed uncertainty is not added.

E6.justification: The original Table 1 scores remain unchanged, but v3 adds ConvCNP results, two kernel-comparison columns per metric, and coupling/trace-estimator findings. Table 2 newly reports OFM SMSE/MSLL of 0.29/0.087 for Gibbs and 0.21/0.094 for Rational Quadratic GPs. Tables 7–8 substantially extend the measured results rather than demonstrate improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds explicit Gaussian-measure and Cameron–Martin-space definitions and the translated-measure equivalence/singularity theorem. Most substantive derivations are retained or relocated: Proposition 3.1 and Appendix I restate the Bayesian posterior derivation already present in v1.

C1.justification: The central claims about learned stochastic-process priors, tractable densities, and functional regression remain. The introduction explicitly broadens the claimed first extension to stochastic interpolants and rectified flow alongside flow matching; most other contribution bullets restate existing capabilities.

C2.justification: New Appendix A distinguishes formulation error from finite-data/model approximation, qualifies the supremum-to-expectation relaxation, and explains evaluation and baseline-selection limitations. Sections 3.1 and Appendix P add interpretations of coupling and estimator behavior, while Appendix Q proposes computational mitigations. Low-dimensional and computational limitations already present in v1 are retained, with larger data requirements newly acknowledged.

D1.justification: Appendix N specifies the new Gibbs kernel parameters and the scikit-learn Rational Quadratic implementation with length-scale 0.15; Appendix P documents the added diagnostic settings. Existing hardware, training budgets, SGLD parameters, solver tolerances, and code address are retained. Moving the solver disclosure to Appendix O is not a new implementation detail.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations and discussion of ConvCNP, stochastic interpolants, rectified flow, and efficient operators/solvers, plus explicit positioning against fixed-grid inpainting and Table 9's OFM/NP comparison. The main relationships to OPFLOW, COT-FM, functional flow matching, and neural processes remain; the Fjelde flow-matching blog citation is removed.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: v1 Section 3.1 moves to Appendix F, the Bayesian derivation moves to Appendix I, and the appendices become separately lettered sections. New questions-and-answers, background explanations, contribution bullets, and a plain-language framework summary materially expand the exposition.

P2.justification: v3 adds the framework diagram in Figure 1, estimator plots in Figure 25, and Tables 2 and 7–9. Regression figures gain ConvCNP panels, while existing figures receive revised panel labels, captions, and arrangements. Table emphasis and the overall conference layout also change; the original visual evidence is largely retained.

improvement.justification: The added ConvCNP comparisons, kernel tests, and direct coupling/trace diagnostics strengthen the empirical support, while the new explanations clarify approximation and applicability. These gains are qualified: uncertainty across repeated main-benchmark runs remains unreported, and Appendix P overgeneralizes scaling benefits—Table 7 reports 182 function evaluations at batch size 128 versus 168 for independent coupling. The evidence supports a positive but limited overall improvement.
